questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Explain the difference between

(i) Data verification and data validation. (2 marks)

(ii) Length check and range check. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Verification and validation (2 marks).** **Data verification** checks that the data entered is the same as the original source data, that is, that it has been copied correctly (for example by double entry, where the data is typed twice and compared, or by proofreading against the source document). **Data validation** is an automatic check done by the computer program to see that the data entered is reasonable and acceptable (sensible, of the right type and within the allowed limits); it cannot prove that the data is the correct value, only that it is possible.

**(ii) Length check and range check (2 marks).** A **length check** tests that the number of characters entered in a field is the required one or within a set limit (for example a phone number must have 9 digits). A **range check** tests that a numeric (or date) value lies between a given minimum and maximum (for example a mark must be between 0 and 20).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Briefly describe what is meant by:

(i) Video conferencing (2 marks)

(ii) E-commerce (2 marks)

(iii) Network protocol (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Video conferencing (2 marks).** It is a communication service that uses computers or phones with a camera, microphone, screen and speakers connected through a network (the Internet) to let people in different places see and hear each other in real time and hold a meeting without travelling.

**(ii) E-commerce (2 marks).** Electronic commerce is the buying and selling of goods and services, and the payment for them, over the Internet or other computer networks (for example online shopping and mobile money payment).

**(iii) Network protocol (2 marks).** A network protocol is an agreed set of rules and conventions that governs how data is formatted, addressed, sent and received between devices on a network, so that different devices can communicate (examples: TCP/IP, HTTP, FTP, SMTP).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) (i) What is computer simulation? (1 mark)

(ii) Describe an advantage of computer simulation in bridge construction. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Computer simulation (1 mark).** Computer simulation is the use of a computer program to build a model of a real-life system or process and to imitate its behaviour, so that it can be studied and its results predicted without using the real thing.

**(ii) Advantage in bridge construction (2 marks).** Engineers can test the design of the bridge on the computer under different loads, winds, floods or earthquakes before building it. Weak points are found and corrected early, which saves the cost of building and testing real models, avoids danger to people, and makes it quick and cheap to try other designs.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) (i) The download rate on a certain connection is 64Kb per second. Find how long it takes to download a 2MB file over this connection. (3 marks)

(ii) Determine the exact storage capacity of a 4GB USB key in kilobytes. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Download time (3 marks).** The rate is given in kilobits (Kb) per second, whereas the file size is in megabytes (MB), so the units must be made the same.

- 2 MB = 2 × 1024 KB = 2048 KB (kilobytes)
- 1 byte = 8 bits, so 2048 KB = 2048 × 8 = 16 384 Kb (kilobits)
- Time = size ÷ rate = 16 384 Kb ÷ 64 Kb per second = **256 seconds**

256 s = 4 minutes 16 seconds.

(If "Kb" were read as kilobytes, the time would be 2048 ÷ 64 = 32 seconds; but a capital K with a small b means kilobits, hence 256 seconds. Using 1 MB = 1000 KB would give 250 seconds. Computed by script.)

**(ii) Capacity of a 4GB USB key (4 marks).** "Exact" means that the binary multiples are used: 1 GB = 1024 MB and 1 MB = 1024 KB.

- 4 GB = 4 × 1024 MB = 4096 MB
- 4096 MB = 4096 × 1024 KB = **4 194 304 KB**

(In one step: 4 × 1024 × 1024 = 4 194 304 kilobytes.)
